newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ferrari pretax profit zooms ahead in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ferrari pretax profit zooms ahead in 1996.

text.p: Luxury Italian sportscar maker Ferrari said on Thursday its 1996 pretax profits accelerated to triple the levels of the previous year and it expected sales to speed ahead in 1997 as well.

Ferrari, in a statement from its Maranello headquarters near the northern Italian city of Modena, said pretax profits rose to 12 billion lire ($7.19 million) compared with 3.8 billion the previous year.
Sales shot up 20 percent to 878 billion due mainly to the success of its two new models the 550 Maranello and the 456 GTA automatic.

Ferrari chairman Luca di Montezemolo said sales in the first few months of 1997 remained at high levels on its principle world markets and these allowed the company to expect "further significant growth in turnover for the current year."

The group, which exports 87 percent of its vehicles, had showed significant growth in its main market the United States and in Japan, while in Switzerland and in its second export market, Germany, results were particularly positive.

As far as its Formula One motor racing activities were concerned, "continuation of the results achieved in competitions up to the present are the principle objective for the rest of the season," it said.
Ferrari is currently leading the Formula One constructors' and drivers' championships after taking first and third place at last Sunday's Monaco Grand Prix.
